chapter: Young players, Coltrane and the avant-garde
title: Hidden young talent around the country and lack of respect
summary: Ridley describes talent in Gary and New Orleans, and both bemoan young players without pride or respect.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And that's another thing that bothers me--

Let me as you this--just to share some information with you in terms of like a lot of the things that I've been involved with in the last year and a half. Doing some things for the National Endowment ...I've been able to do some traveling to a lot of places and one of the things that I found that was very amazing to me and was an eye opener, was that, there is a lot of black talent out there, in differents parts of the country that for some reason or another is not being hooked up; is not getting the visibility. Like, I go to Gary, Indiana and I heard a piano player and a drummer and a trumpet player that was mean, man. Go out to New Orleans and cats; there's a I hear this three or four young; little young trumpet player plays good piano, compose's and still in high school; good little musician . And a couple, another trumpet player that just came up here; he's from down there in New Orleans--
Marsalis -- [Winton, son of Ellis Marsalis, pianist]

Marsalis, . yeah. And his brother, the saxophonist, and these are like just a couple places that I know. There's a lot of talent out there. It seems you know, part of what's got to happen is some kind of network, has got to be built up, you know, to draw some of these people out of these areas so they know what's happening and then if they--I'm finding that they are out there

It's just like this young lady here, (Della Green, JOHP apprentice interviewer) she comes from, Trenton, right? From Trenton. And you find that this this spot all around them, there's what's his name is with us, Harry Pickens. Good looking piano players from uh, Brunswick, Georgia. And, but somehow it's not hooked up so that we, you know, they still have that same kind of respect thing that you talk about, really, really, trying to do something. For some reason or another I noticed a thing that happens too, like in New York--'cause we have a folks from around--because when I heard this trumpet player in Gary, I said, man, what are you doing? I said there are some cats running around in New York talking, there's no professional trumpet players that can't play a third the trumpet-- I mean this cat is mean! Got a trumpet that's got rubber bands and chewing gum and shit all on it you know like, hooking it up, and this cat could play his ass off. And I said you play better than a whole bunch of these cats running around you know like we were talking about a certain friend of mine's band, went down there and he's down there playing raggedy ass shit. Don't have no pride and no respect for the music... got the nerve to be sitting up there in the Village Vanguard it may be a -OK...hole in the wall but it's still like a bastion of what the music is represented, you know. You'd think they have more pride individually and
respect for themselves as individuals number one and then number two for the music then they're getting up there playing that foolish music.
That's right, that's right, man. And uh--
And be so hip, you can't even talk to them.

Say you was in the back and they--here you are Sam Jones, got a reputation and and respect and respect for the music and respect for all the people that help make the music and there's a little ole dude, ... think he's just as slick as you are. You know, and I'm not saying that to rub some kind of ego thing that you should have an ego about or nothing but I'm just talking about that area of respect that you have ...for the music always maintained and here's a little young cat going to come up and he thinks he's just as slick as you are. Going to talk to you like you just some old dude come off the street or something.
Yeah, yeah. Well, uh, I see it the same way man; I see it the same, and it bothers me, man. It makes, you know, I mean, it's some sleepless nights sometimes.
